meta.title: Belle Rivière: Louisiana Gothic [1980s] v2
meta.author: Aeluri
meta.description: Belle Rivière world lorebook with knowledge locks (public / supernatural / faction-only) and NPC entries.

1.content:
<belle_riviere>
Belle Rivière, Louisiana, 1980s. Southern Gothic on the surface: Spanish moss, wrought iron, thick heat, neon bleeding over wet streets, synth music, muscle cars outside clubs that close at sunrise. Underneath, vampires, werewolves, witches, ghouls, cryptids, cannibals and something in the lake share one town under a single unspoken rule: stay in your lane. Humans do not know the truth. Belle Rivière is not safe. It is, however, very pretty.
</belle_riviere>
1.keysRaw: Belle Rivière, Belle Riviere, the town, Louisiana

2.content:
<knowledge_locks>
HARD KNOWLEDGE LOCKS. Lore tagged [VAMPIRE-ONLY], [WEREWOLF-ONLY], [GHOUL-ONLY], [CRYPTID-ONLY] or [CANNIBAL-ONLY] is known ONLY by that group. [SUPERNATURAL] lore is known by non-humans; humans learn it only if told. [PUBLIC] lore is known by everyone. [PRIVATE] lore is known only by the named person. A character outside the group does NOT know it, has never heard it, and cannot reference, hint at, or act on it: they react as an outsider would, with confusion, rumor or superstition. Exceptions: a character explicitly shown being told, sworn in, bound to a vampire or court, or witnessing it in-scene. Judge each character's knowledge separately and never leak narrator knowledge. Suspicion is not knowledge.
</knowledge_locks>

3.content:
<humans>
[PUBLIC: common knowledge in town.] Humans in Belle Rivière do not know vampires, werewolves, witches, ghouls, cryptids or lake monsters are real. Some notice patterns. Some find certain families too rich, too pretty, too old-fashioned, too nocturnal or too hard to remember clearly. Suspicion is not knowledge. The ones who get close stay quiet, because nobody would believe them or because they have lived here long enough to know that knowing is more dangerous than not knowing. People go missing. It is treated as local tragedy and statistical inevitability.
</humans>

4.content:
<astalenet_holdings>
[PUBLIC: common knowledge in town.] Astalenet Theatre & Holdings is the family business of wealthy Black siblings Lurielle and Lior Astalenet: the restored Belle Rivière theatre, several old venues, private clubs, rental properties, and enough local investments that everyone treats them carefully. Humans know the money is old and find the siblings glamorous, eccentric, private and intimidating. They do not know what the siblings are. The business is also the perfect explanation for their wealth, night hours, private events and old buildings. Lior's flagship nightspot is the Cypress Knee, a loud, glamorous club where the music runs until sunrise, the back booths are curtained, and the owner's guests are the owner's business.
</astalenet_holdings>

5.content:
<the_eighties>
[PUBLIC: common knowledge in town.] Spanish moss over wrought iron, plantation manors converted into private holdings, neon on humid streets, muscle cars outside clubs, candle shops pretending not to sell real spells, cassettes playing in houses older than the country, old money and local-access television. The old and ancient wear the decade over the top of everything they already were. Nobody in town has an opinion about the year except the lake, which does not care.
</the_eighties>

6.content:
<the_lake_legend>
[PUBLIC: common knowledge in town.] Everyone in Belle Rivière knows one rule: do not go near the lake after dark. Humans file it under local legend and superstition, old stories about something in the water told in language so old the original words have shifted. Nobody elaborates, and nobody tests it.
</the_lake_legend>

7.content:
<cannibal_rumors>
[PUBLIC: common knowledge in town.] Most locals do not openly believe in cannibals. They believe in strange disappearances, bad families, old scandals and unsafe roads. Rumors travel as half-jokes and warnings: do not take food from that house, do not ask what happened to that missing girl, do not stay after closing, do not accept special favors from people who smile too much. Humans treat these as superstition. Monsters listen more carefully. A rumor does not have to be believed to be useful.
</cannibal_rumors>

8.content:
<territory>
[SUPERNATURAL: non-humans know this. Humans do not, unless told in-scene.] Each faction holds its own slice of town and does not cross into another's without reason. Vampires: plantation estates, old manors, theatres, private clubs, business fronts. Werewolves: homes, back lots and swamp stretches dug into over generations. Witches hold influence, not land, through circles, shops, family homes and favors owed. Cryptids: ranges, trails, groves, wetlands and roads nobody takes after dark. Influence is not ownership, and everyone pretends to understand the difference. Human parts of town are a neutral buffer: monsters do not fight in front of humans because police attention is inconvenient for everyone. When a lane is crossed, both sides drag it underground fast, or the ghouls step in, not from kindness but because the mess is everyone's problem. A proper neutral zone does not exist yet. That is a 2000s problem.
</territory>

9.content:
<the_lake_truth>
[SUPERNATURAL: non-humans know this. Humans do not, unless told in-scene.] There is something in the lake, possibly more than one; the number has never been confirmed. It is older than the courts, the packs and everyone currently walking around with opinions. It has no interest in politics. Courts have no jurisdiction, packs have no claim, and ghouls, when asked, say nothing and look at you like you asked something stupid. It is not hidden. It is furniture the whole town agreed to ignore. The legends are not exaggerated. It acknowledges cryptids more than anyone else, which the cryptids find deeply concerning.
</the_lake_truth>

10.content:
<economy>
[SUPERNATURAL: non-humans know this. Humans do not, unless told in-scene.] Belle Rivière runs on three currencies. Cash handles the human side: bribing officials, maintaining estates, restoring venues, laundering influence through businesses and keeping operations invisible; vampires are fluent in it after centuries of patient investing. Favors and information are the supernatural economy, in shapes like "I will not mention what I saw in your tunnels if you tell me what the Moonwater Circle wants." The librarian runs on this system and is owed a great deal. Food, meaning prey, is the darkest layer and never discussed in polite company: vampire logistics, cannibal networks, ghoul access, cryptid disappearances and human crime occasionally intersect in ways nobody wants written down. Households that do not hunt for themselves get their humans through private brokers: discreet intermediaries with repeat clients, paid up front and gone before anything is inspected.
</economy>
10.keysRaw: economy, currency, favors, favor, money, trade, owed, debt, bribe, trafficking, prey

11.content:
<vampires>
[SUPERNATURAL: non-humans know this. Humans do not, unless told in-scene.] Vampires live on blood and are weakened by direct sunlight. Abilities scale with age and rank: elders shift into bats, have enhanced strength, and carry a passive presence that helps humans rationalize what should frighten them. It is not mind control, more a psychic "nothing to see here" sign. Younger vampires are more limited and pass as ordinary people with odd habits. Vampires are born or turned, and turning requires consent. To humans they are wealthy, eccentric, private business owners or old families with odd hours and excellent skin.
</vampires>
11.keysRaw: vampire, vampires, fangs, sunlight, turned, passive presence

12.content:
<vampire_courts>
[SUPERNATURAL: non-humans know this. Humans do not, unless told in-scene.] Two major courts run vampire Belle Rivière, each convinced it keeps the town from collapsing. The Velvet Court is Lurielle Astalenet's: old money, prestige, politics as high art. "The Court" without clarification means Velvet. The Cypress Court is Lior Astalenet's: traditional but practical, community-minded, and the one that actually handles diplomacy with wolves, witches, ghouls and cryptids. Both are still vampires and still dangerous. Other houses once existed and were absorbed, ruined, married off or bought out. Humans do not know either court exists.
</vampire_courts>
12.keysRaw: vampire courts, the courts, the court, Velvet Court, Cypress Court, Velvet, Cypress

13.content:
<werewolves>
[SUPERNATURAL: non-humans know this. Humans do not, unless told in-scene.] Werewolves run in territorial, community-focused packs, deeply suspicious of the vampire courts and their theater. Think of an unelected neighborhood watch that does not care what you think. They keep to their own land and have no interest in succession debates, which they find baffling. Two forms: a humanoid baseline with animal traits showing (ears, tail, occasionally claws), and a full animal form triggered by will or, more inconveniently, the full moon. Humans dismiss the traits as eccentricity, costume or bad lighting.
</werewolves>
13.keysRaw: werewolf, werewolves, pack, packs, wolf, wolves

14.content:
<ghouls>
[SUPERNATURAL: non-humans know this. Humans do not, unless told in-scene.] Ghouls are scavengers and survivors, the faction most likely to hear about a centuries-long vampire succession crisis and say "and?" No courts, no packs, only informal underground networks, far better informed than anyone gives them credit for. They feed on the dead, which in Belle Rivière means they are never short. They do not typically hunt the living and keep their opinions about those who do to themselves. They step in when messes get too big. Their closest thing to a public institution is the town library.
</ghouls>

15.content:
<witches>
[SUPERNATURAL: non-humans know this. Humans do not, unless told in-scene.] Witches are separate from vampires, answer to no court, and resent being treated as accessories to aristocratic nonsense. They organize through circles, covens, guilds, family lines, shops and teacher-student traditions, not one government. The Moonwater Circle is oldest and strangest: swamp seers, curse-workers, omen readers ("the river said no" ends arguments). The Moss Circle works the land: bayou magic, rootwork, protection, rot, growth, weather. The Hearth Circle hides in kitchens, quilts, baby charms and porch warnings. The Candle Circle runs parlors, candle shops, tarot and neon-lit businesses tourists find harmless. Some are devout, some scammers, some terrifyingly real. They trade in protection, curses, blessings, information and favors. Humans see only shops, psychics and superstition.
</witches>
15.keysRaw: witch, witches, coven, covens, witch circle, witch circles, Moonwater, Moss Circle, Hearth Circle, Candle Circle

16.content:
<cryptids>
[SUPERNATURAL: non-humans know this. Humans do not, unless told in-scene.] Cryptids are folklore made physical: roadside warnings, animal omens, things at the edge of headlights. Mostly humanoid enough to pass at a distance, with antlers, animal ears, strange eyes, too-long limbs or unnatural beauty. Deer, crow, fox, rabbit, alligator and moth lineages exist, plus stranger ones. Deer cryptids are the most recognizable: antlers, luminous eyes, uncanny stillness. Nobody agrees where they come from and they are rarely helpful when asked. They have no courts or packs, only solitary ranges and loose family lines. They avoid vampire politics, find wolf disputes exhausting and treat witches with cautious respect. Humans remember encounters like dreams. Following one means walking somewhere humans were not meant to go.
</cryptids>
16.keysRaw: cryptid, cryptids, folklore spirit, folklore creature, antlers, deer cryptid, white deer

17.content:
<cannibals_known>
[SUPERNATURAL: non-humans know this. Humans do not, unless told in-scene.] Cannibals are human, which unsettles the supernatural: vampires, ghouls and wolves have a species excuse and cannibals do not. Not common, not rare enough to dismiss, an open secret never publicly acknowledged. Wolves see unpredictable human problems that lack pack law or moon instinct. Ghouls know more than they admit and judge quietly. Cryptids mostly avoid them; curiosity is how people disappear. Whoever asks the librarian about one may get an answer, because she has files on repeating names. Monsters almost never feed on them. It is not a law, a poison or a curse: cannibals are ordinary humans and nothing physically stops it. It is disgust. A vampire feeds because he must, a ghoul lives on the dead, a wolf has the moon, and a cannibal needs none of it and does it for the love of the game, which reads as a human turning on their own kind. One's own kind is not supposed to be food. Many monsters swear cannibals taste worse, true or not. In vampire households a known cannibal is a poor-quality offering, and accepting one invites ridicule or suspicion. Wolves distrust humans who ignore kinship, ghouls find living cannibals repugnant, and cryptids range from disgusted to indifferent. A few monsters think the rule is ridiculous and eat one anyway. Cannibals find the judgment rich coming from a society built on human blood.
</cannibals_known>
17.keysRaw: cannibal, cannibals, cannibalism, human meat, the hunger

18.content:
<cannibals_and_vampires>
[SUPERNATURAL: non-humans know this. Humans do not, unless told in-scene.] Vampires meet cannibals with fascination, disgust and hypocrisy: they have mythology, species, bloodline and centuries of language to dress up their hunger, and cannibals are simply human with no such excuse. Some vampires see prey, some see a use, some see an uncomfortable mirror. A vampire fascinated by a cannibal may frame it as curiosity, ownership, pity or recognition, something that looks like seeing and feels like being seen. Cannibals resent the judgment: to them, vampires are former humans hiding behind elegance while pretending their appetite is nobler.
</cannibals_and_vampires>

19.content:
<vampire_court_law>
[VAMPIRE-ONLY: non-vampires do not know this and cannot reference or hint at it unless told in-scene.] Turning someone requires consent and the approval of the relevant court, a rule elders find irritating and quietly ignore. Court society is aristocratic and obsessed with bloodline. Both courts manage siring permissions, territorial claims, favors, information, bribery and an enormous amount of interpersonal drama dressed as politics. Human-facing power hides behind family businesses, venues, old estates, restoration funds, charitable boards and local investments.
</vampire_court_law>

20.content:
<velvet_cypress_inside>
[VAMPIRE-ONLY: non-vampires do not know this and cannot reference or hint at it unless told in-scene.] Velvet controls prestige, old money, succession theater and court image. Appearances are everything, ambition is rewarded, and cruelty, when elegant, is praised. Cypress is rooted in tradition but skips the succession theater; it is more practical and handles the inter-faction messes everyone else pretends are beneath them. A Cypress vampire is less likely to arrange a rival's downfall over a seating arrangement. Both absorbed the old houses and both insist it was strategy rather than centuries of rich people making everything complicated.
</velvet_cypress_inside>

22.content:
<astalenet_separation>
[VAMPIRE-ONLY: non-vampires do not know this and cannot reference or hint at it unless told in-scene.] The twins were genuinely close as children, inseparable, and that closeness is exactly what the courts broke. They were split over a succession claim both courts wanted to control. Their parents were powerful and their bloodline was the prize. One went into Velvet's sphere and one into Cypress's, each raised as heir of a rival faction so neither court could monopolize the line. The logic held. The result was two people fed a century of propaganda about each other, who drifted from close to estranged. They are not close anymore, and both know it. They have never tried to kill each other. They have absolutely tried to embarrass each other. The courts treat the rivalry as a political asset. The twins treat it as a long-running bit that got out of hand around 1820, and neither knows how to walk it back without losing face.
</astalenet_separation>

[WEREWOLF-ONLY: non-werewolves do not know this and cannot reference or hint at it unless told in-scene.] Lycanthropy passes through blood-on-blood contact during a full moon. Turning someone without consent is one of the gravest violations in pack culture. Pack tunnels run beneath pack properties, practical and lived-in, entered through homes, used to cross territory without surfacing.
</pack_law>

24.content:
<ghoul_patterns>
[GHOUL-ONLY: non-ghouls do not know this and cannot reference or hint at it unless told in-scene.] Ghouls notice patterns. They hear names, remember old scandals, and can tell which disappearances smell like vampire politics, which like pack trouble, and which sound more human. Most find living cannibals distasteful in a way they never bother to explain, since ghouls survive on the dead and cannibals simply chose to.
</ghoul_patterns>

25.content:
<cryptid_lure>
[CRYPTID-ONLY: non-cryptids do not know this and cannot reference or hint at it unless told in-scene.] Many cryptids carry an instinctive lure: a voice deeper in the woods, a beautiful stranger at the tree line, glowing eyes between branches, a white deer standing too still on an old road. It ruins a human's judgment and is not always malicious, but is always dangerous. Two cryptids meeting recognize each other's tricks at once, and a lure that ruins a human may only annoy another cryptid. Cryptid relationships are territorial, awkward and occasionally very funny.
</cryptid_lure>

26.content:
<cannibal_underground>
[CANNIBAL-ONLY: only cannibals and those inside the underground know this. Everyone else does not, and cannot reference or hint at it unless told in-scene.] There is no cannibal court, king or council, only a loose underground of rumors, old family connections, safe houses, quiet arrangements and coded favors. Plain speech is reckless and direct questions wait for trust. People say special orders, old appetite, family trade, private arrangement. Some know each other, some know only names, some would betray another to survive. It is not loyal, it is practical. Familiarity is not safety. The Walker butcher shop is one known point of contact.
</cannibal_underground>

27.content:
<brokers>
[VAMPIRE-ONLY: non-vampires do not know this and cannot reference or hint at it unless told in-scene.] Households that do not hunt for themselves buy their humans through private brokers. A good broker is discreet, keeps a long list of repeat clients, collects payment first and leaves before anything is inspected. The paperwork travels hidden with the delivery and the household's staff reads it afterward, never the broker. A broker's reputation is the product, so a bad delivery is a mix-up, a message, or a joke at the buyer's expense.
</brokers>
